Trübner | language = German}} was the second phase of the [[Armenian language]], spoken and written in between the 12th and 18th centuries, after [[Classical Armenian|Grabar]] (Classical Armenian) and before [[Armenian language|Ashkharhabar]] (Modern Armenian).{{cite book | last = Melkonian | first = Zareh | script-title=hy:Գործնական Քերականութիւն - Արդի Հայերէն Լեզուի (Միջին եւ Բարձրագոյն Դասընթացք) | edition = Fourth | year = 1990 | location = [[Los Angeles]] | language = Armenian | page=137}} Classical Armenian was predominantly an inflecting and synthetic language; in Middle Armenian, agglutinative and analytical forms influenced the language.''History of the Armenian Language in the Pre-Written Period'', Yerevan, 1987. In this respect, Middle Armenian is a transition stage from Old Armenian to Modern Armenian (Ashkharhabar).H. Acharian, History of the Armenian Language, parts I-II Middle Armenian introduced the letters [[O (Armenian letter)|օ]] (o) and [[Fe (Armenian letter)|ֆ]] (fe), based on the Greek letters "o" and "φ". == Additions == The letter [[O (Armenian letter)|օ]], based on the Greek letter [[O (Greek)|o]], was added during this period. It originally represented the IPA sound {{IPA|/o/}} ([[close-mid back rounded vowel]]), which developed out of the [[Classical Armenian#Phonology|Classical Armenian diphthong]] աւ {{IPA|/ɑw/}}. Today, in the [[Armenian alphabet]], it represents IPA {{IPA|/ↄ/}} ([[open-mid back rounded vowel]]) and is indistinguishable in most cases from ո. Therefore, in standard orthography, o is only written word-initially (using ո represents the cluster {{IPA|/vↄ/}} initially). The letter [[Fe (Armenian letter)|ֆ]], based on the Greek letter [[Phi|φ]], was added during this period. It represents the IPA sound {{IPA|/f/}} ([[voiceless labiodental fricative]]), which is [[Classical_Armenian#Consonants|not a native phoneme in Armenian.]] However, it was prevalent in borrowed words, making it necessary to use a letter to write it. It is still used today in the [[Armenian alphabet]].{{cite book |last=Dum-Tragut |first=Jasmine |year=2009 |title=Armenian: Modern Eastern Armenian |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SGyop5guXDkC&pg=PA18 |publisher=John Benjamins Publishing Company |page=18 |isbn=9789027238146 |access-date=19 May 2021}} == References == {{Reflist}} == External links == * [http://www.nayiri.com/imagedDictionaryBrowser.jsp?dictionaryId=56 Dictionary of Middle Armenian] (Միջին Հայերենի Բառարան), Ruben Ghazarian, Yerevan, 2009. {{Armenian language}} [[Category:Armenian languages]] [[Category:Languages attested from the 12th century]] {{Armenia-stub}}
